content.text: I want to explore a slack experience where I ask clanker that I want to buy shorts like this (image for ref) and it presents me a carousel of shorts that are similar to the one I refered. what are the components here that I'd hv to get right first of all and feasibility of this experience when using slack
I’ll use the **i-have-adhd** skill to keep this easy to scan. I’ll check Slack’s UI limits and Clanker’s current image handling, then map out the pieces this experience needs.
Slack’s current docs include a **native horizontal carousel**, so the UI you described is feasible. The harder part is finding shorts that match the photo’s style and are actually available to buy.

**Yes, this is feasible in Slack, including a real horizontal carousel.** Slack supports **1–10 cards**, with product images, text and buttons. Each card can have up to three buttons. [Carousel docs](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/blocks/carousel-block/), [card docs](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/blocks/card-block/).

The biggest challenge is **finding convincing, purchasable matches**. These are the five components to get right:

1. **Understand what “like this” means.**  
   Identify the shorts within the photo and extract colour, pattern, cut, length, pockets and waistband. A full outfit photo needs the right garment isolated. Budget, size and shopping region come from the conversation; the image cannot establish those.

2. **Find real product candidates.**  
   Choose between searching broadly across the web or searching selected retailers’ catalogs. Broad search gives reach; selected catalogs give more predictable product data. A visual-search provider can help retrieve candidates, while Clanker’s browser can inspect merchant pages.

3. **Rank by visual similarity.**  
   Compare candidate product images with the reference, alongside the extracted attributes. Searching only for “green shorts” will miss differences in silhouette and details. The ranking should support refinements like **“same shape, different colour”** or **“more like the second one.”**

4. **Check whether the results are useful to buy.**  
   Connect each image to the correct product and variant. Verify the merchant link, observed price, available sizes and delivery region where possible. Show unknown availability honestly and remove duplicate listings.

5. **Make the Slack interaction feel continuous.**  
   Present perhaps five cards containing **photo, product name, price, retailer and why it matches**. Use buttons such as **View product**, **More like this** and **Save**. Preserve the reference and preferences within the thread. Button clicks need acknowledgement within three seconds; searching can continue asynchronously. [Interaction docs](https://docs.slack.dev/interactivity/handling-user-interaction/).

For **Clanker specifically**, the code already has [Slack image intake](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/hermes/plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py:4936), vision routing and interactive message infrastructure. The substantial additions are **product retrieval, similarity ranking, product verification and carousel rendering**. I didn’t find an existing shopping recommendation pipeline.

The first version I’d aim for is:

**Photo + request → five similar products → carousel → “cheaper” / “more like this” → merchant page.**

Validate that with a small set of varied reference photos, judging resemblance, working product links, response time and desktop/mobile rendering. Completing checkout adds a separate layer of login, cart and payment work; Clanker’s docs currently record Indian card payments as a [POC limitation](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/docs/ACCESS_MANAGEMENT.md:67).

**Slack’s platform supports the experience; Clanker’s actual carousel rendering and shopping quality still need end-to-end validation.**
